domain: International Humanitarian Law / Law of Armed Conflict
topic_summary: Analysis of Common Article 3 of the 1949 Geneva Conventions, which establishes minimum humanitarian standards for non-international armed conflicts. The kernel is contested between state-centric readings limiting application to traditional wars and expansive readings applying humanitarian constraints broadly to any organized violence, fundamentally disagreeing on the scope of protected persons and constrained actors.

key_entities: Common Article 3 (treaty text establishing minimum humanitarian rules)
Non-state armed groups (insurgents, militias, organized opposition)
International tribunals (ICTY, ICTR, ICC interpreting CA3 scope)
NGO monitoring bodies (ICRC, HRW interpreting compliance)
key_tensions: State sovereignty vs humanitarian constraint (governments vs international law)
Security operations vs due process (counterinsurgency vs detainee rights)

axes.structural_delta: CA3 applies only to conflicts meeting intensity and organization thresholds, excluding routine law enforcement and low-level insurgency
axes.primary_observable: Judicial/treaty body determinations of 'armed conflict not of an international character'; state invocation of domestic law vs IHL
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; instantiates narrow constraint scope with high suppression

axes.human_readable: Expansive Human Rights Reading (Maximum Protection Interpretation)
axes.structural_delta: CA3 applies to any organized armed violence, extending minimum humanitarian standards to detention, interrogation, and military operations regardless of conflict classification
axes.primary_observable: NGO reports treating CA3 as floor for all security operations; tribunal rulings applying CA3 below traditional armed conflict threshold
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; instantiates broad constraint scope, structurally distinct victim/beneficiary set

axes.human_readable: ICRC Customary Law Reading (Practice-Based Middle Ground)
axes.structural_delta: CA3 scope determined by state practice and opinio juris rather than textual interpretation, tracking evolving customary international law
axes.primary_observable: ICRC Customary IHL Study citations; frequency of state acceptance of CA3 obligations in sub-threshold conflicts
axes.selection_reason: Third reading instantiating coordination mechanism between first two readings; structurally distinct as procedural rather than substantive constraint

axes.human_readable: Non-State Actor Agency (Rebel Groups as Rights-Holders)
axes.structural_delta: Whether armed groups can invoke CA3 protections without state recognition, or whether protections flow only from state obligations
axes.primary_observable: Judicial decisions on armed group standing; rebel manifestos citing CA3
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: downstream of expansive reading, lower centrality, scaffolding role rather than core interpretive constraint

axes.human_readable: Detention Authority Gap (CA3 Rights Without Corresponding Powers)
axes.structural_delta: CA3 prohibits inhumane treatment but does not explicitly authorize detention, creating legal vacuum for non-international conflicts
axes.primary_observable: Litigation over detention authority in NIAC contexts; state invocation of inherent authority vs treaty silence
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: high epsilon but downstream entanglement of both readings rather than independent axis; captured via reading-level analysis

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Whether armed groups can invoke CA3 protections without state recognition
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Downstream of expansive reading; scaffolding role rather than core interpretive constraint; lower centrality

deferred_axes.deferral_reason: High epsilon but downstream entanglement of both readings rather than independent axis; captured via reading-level constraint analysis

omegas.description: Is CA3 scope fixed by 1949 treaty text (mountain) or evolving through interpretation (rope)? If fixed but contested, the kernel is stable but interpretive authority itself becomes the constraint.

State-centric reading shields government actions from international prosecution while exposing rebel groups. Does this asymmetry reveal tangled_rope beneficiary structure in supposedly neutral treaty language?
At what duration/intensity does violence trigger CA3? State-centric requires protracted conflict; expansive applies immediately. This threshold determination is itself a concealed high-epsilon axis.
omegas.source: Absence Inventory (threshold mechanics not explicit in either reading)

omegas.description: How does CA3 interact with occupation law (Geneva Convention IV)? Deferred axis detention_authority_gap suggests this interface may warrant independent generation.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel structure confirmed: three readings instantiate genuinely different constraints (narrow vs broad scope vs procedural coordination). Axiom contradictions declared for state_centric vs expansive pair.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Common Article 3 of 1949 Geneva Conventions: treaty text establishing minimum humanitarian standards for 'armed conflict not of an international character'
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: International tribunals, ICRC, state parties, and domestic courts claiming interpretive authority via treaty law, customary IHL, or sovereignty

readings.commitment: CA3 applies only when conflict meets intensity and organization thresholds, excluding low-level violence and law enforcement
readings.authority_grounding: State sovereignty; treaty interpretation favoring narrow construction of obligations
readings.expected_structural_delta: High suppression of constraint application; irregular combatants below threshold excluded from victim set; governments retain maximum operational discretion

readings.commitment: CA3 applies to any organized armed violence as floor of minimum humanitarian standards regardless of classification
readings.authority_grounding: International human rights law; evolutionary treaty interpretation; tribunal jurisprudence
readings.expected_structural_delta: Broad constraint application; all detainees and affected populations enter victim set; state security operations face external monitoring and potential prosecution

readings.commitment: CA3 scope determined by evolving state practice and opinio juris tracked through customary international law
readings.authority_grounding: ICRC as guardian of IHL; state practice evidence; multilateral acceptance
readings.expected_structural_delta: Procedural constraint on interpretation rather than substantive scope; coordination mechanism allowing gradual expansion without formal treaty amendment

axiom_contradictions.basis: State-centric grounds authority in sovereign discretion to classify conflicts and limits external constraint; expansive grounds authority in universal human dignity requiring external constraint regardless of state classification. No single framework can hold both sovereignty-as-interpretive-authority and universal-rights-as-interpretive-authority simultaneously.
